trainingPlans.name: Lunchtime Strength and Outdoor Running - November to May
trainingPlans.source: Ambitious conditional treadmill progression rebuilt on 8 November 2026 using the user-estimated baseline of 3 x 5 minutes at 7.0 km/h. First week verifies tolerance. All steps are time-based with explicit km/h. Original planName retained for replacement-import identity; strength workouts, dates and exclusions retained. Targets are coaching estimates, not promised outcomes; progression requires successful prior stages.

goal.primaryGoal: Build from 3 x 5 minutes at 7.0 km/h towards comfortable continuous running, a roughly 10 km treadmill long run by late March, and a conditional sub-30-minute 5K attempt by early May. Optional endurance route towards 12-13 km replaces some speed emphasis. Preserve muscle and pursue strength alongside the separate nutrition plan.
goal.scheduling: Tuesday and Thursday gym at lunchtime (Afternoon); Saturday gym Morning. Monday/Wednesday/Friday runs at lunchtime through 26 March, then Evening from Monday 29 March 2027. Sunday rest. No exact clock time is encoded.
goal.timeBudget: Default sessions: maximum 95.0 minutes including walking. Optional longest: 105 minutes. Early sessions fit lunchtime; longer sessions move to Evening on 29 March as already scheduled.
goal.nutritionContext: Separate nutrition phase: 2700 kcal, protein 200 g, carbs 295 g, fat 80 g initially; use actual trends to adjust. Do not automatically eat back watch calories.
goal.calendarPolicy: Only trip and worktrip events block the actual session slot. Other appointments, social events, birthdays and leave labels are ignored. Christmas Day is explicitly off. Saturday 5 December morning gym fits before the afternoon trip. Calendar export is a snapshot, not a live connection.

checkpoints.target: Confirm 3 x 5 minutes at 7.0 km/h with 2-minute walking recoveries between reps.
Aim for 30 continuous minutes at 7.0 km/h; about 3.5 km, not yet 5 km.
Conditional 45 minutes at 7.5 km/h, approximately 5.6 km; lower belt speed if needed.
Conditional 75 minutes at 8.0 km/h, approximately 10 km; runs switch to Evening.
Speed route: 85-minute easy long run and later 3 x 8-minute reps at 10.1 km/h. Endurance alternative: 95-minute long run and easy Wednesday.
Optional 30 minutes at 10.1 km/h after meeting readiness checks; sub-30 5K is a stretch goal, not an expected result. Otherwise run easy and reassess.

phases.conditioning: Confirm baseline and extend run/walk reps at 7.0 km/h; travel weeks consolidate.

phases.recoveryPriority: Do not increase loads, sets and running duration sharply at the same time.

strengthProgression.startingLoads: Current working loads were not provided. Choose weights that allow the lower end of the rep range with the specified repetitions in reserve. Do not use old personal bests to prescribe load.
strengthProgression.introductoryVolume: 9-15 November: on each workout use 3 sets where 4 are prescribed and 2 where 3 are prescribed; keep 2-set exercises at 2. 16-22 November: restore full upper-body sets if recovered; retain 2 sets for trap-bar deadlift and RDL. From 23 November use the full listed volume if recovery supports it. These are manual adjustments.
strengthProgression.effortTarget: Upper-body lifts and accessories generally 1-2 reps in reserve; squat/deadlift/RDL 2-3. Tuesday squats around 3. No planned failure sets or maximal tests.
strengthProgression.progression: When every working set reaches the upper rep limit with the target reps in reserve and controlled form, add the smallest practical increment, usually 1-2.5 kg for upper body and 2.5-5 kg for lower body. Return towards the low end of the rep range. Track each bench and squat day separately. Maintain rather than force progression when fatigue is high.
strengthProgression.deloadRule: Manual lighter weeks: 14-19 December, 25-30 January, 8-13 March and 19-24 April. Change 4 sets to 2, 3 sets to 2 and 2 sets to 1; lower loads about 10% as needed and keep 4 reps in reserve. These instructions do not automatically alter imported set counts.
strengthProgression.travelReturn: After missed travel sessions, resume with the last successful load rather than making up sets. Saturday 5 December can use reduced sets if travel fatigue warrants it.
strengthProgression.runningInteraction: If lower-body soreness affects running form, remove one squat/hinge working set or make the run easier. After Monday long runs, Tuesday squats stay moderate. Friday evening runs stay short and easy before Saturday morning lifting.
strengthProgression.timeLimit: If a lunch session must be shorter, omit the final accessory before shortening compound-lift rest. Do not rush technique. Allow longer breaks when needed.
strengthProgression.successMeasure: Pursue repetitions and load increases while tracking technique and effort. Maintaining absolute strength while losing weight is also a successful outcome.

readinessRules: Sunday is a full rest day. Christmas Day off. Do not make up missed travel sessions.
Only trips and work trips affect scheduling, matched to the actual session slot. Other calendar events are ignored. Check holiday gym opening hours independently.

Start treadmill running when everyday walking is comfortable. Stop if recurring calf, ankle or shin burning returns; arrange physiotherapy assessment if it recurs. Focal bone tenderness, swelling or pain at rest warrants medical review, especially with previous stress fracture.

Only advance after completing the preceding stage with controlled breathing, no pain during or after, and usual next-morning recovery. If not, repeat the last comfortable stage and shift later sessions manually. Belt speeds are conditional targets, not mandatory minimums. Easy effort must allow full sentences; lower speed if needed without extending time.

Progress after comfortable recent sessions and normal next-morning recovery. Repeat the last successful stage if needed; manually shift later sessions instead of jumping ahead. After a missed week, resume an easier tolerated stage.

Before quicker reps: complete at least two symptom-free weeks containing a continuous 25-30 minute run. Keep quicker work controlled, around 6-7/10 effort, never sprinting. If not ready, use the fallback session instead.
Optional endurance sessions replace Mondays and require an easy Wednesday; follow their ordered progression and retain the 19 April cutback. Choose endurance or the final speed test, not both.
From 29 March all runs are Evening. Friday stays short and easy before Saturday Morning squats; shorten or omit Friday if recovery is inadequate.
Use lighter lifting weeks and lower-running-volume weeks. Persistent fatigue, poor sleep or strength decline calls for reviewing training and energy intake, not automatically adding work.
All running sessions use a treadmill at 0% incline. Use the safety clip, water and suitable running shoes.

All watch steps use time endpoints in seconds. Belt speeds are explicit in labels and speedKmh. Minute fields match the timed steps exactly. Introductory strength volume, deload changes and optional replacements require manual application.

If travel, illness or symptoms interrupt progression, resume the last comfortable stage rather than jumping to the calendar target. Week 1 is a baseline check, not a fitness test. Target dates may move.
